answer.evidence: The backrest has a top band at rows 10-14. At x=8 it runs from L=128 up to a highlight of L=195 at row 13, then a darker edge line at row 14 (#bc9250). Rows 15-16 are darker (L=128), which reads as eave shadow. Below that, a rear face of about 10 rows (16-25) is drawn at full width 14, with darker side posts (x=4, L=103) and light horizontal slat bands at rows 17-18 and 20-21. Rows 26-29 are two legs with a gap between them. The silhouette steps from 12 to 14 pixels wide at row 16, so the body has volume rather than a flat slab. The seat plane itself is mostly hidden behind the backrest because this is a back view, so the top is carried mainly by the backrest cap and the slat bands.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is small, about one tile, and has 7 distinct colours. That is below the bench (14), lamp (14), hedge (11), stall (40) and well (38). Its 7 colours per tile are lower than the hedge (10), stall (17) and well (20). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted brown, a dark tone of the wood, not a black sticker line. The wood has only about 3 visible lightness steps (light slat, mid, dark outline/shadow) against 5-6 in the references. Texture is limited to a few grain and slat-edge dots, with no real wood grain or per-slat highlights. It reads as a clean, plausible chair back but is shallower than the bench and the other references, so a careful artist would see it as thinner next to them. When in doubt, fail.

Below it, rows 16-25 form a 14-wide back face with a darker left column and lighter center slat bands at rows 17-18 and 20-21. Two legs run from rows 26-29, with dark feet at the bottom. The face is 3+ rows, so it is not a flat slab. The seat plane itself is not clearly separate from the back, so the top evidence rests mainly on the backrest top band. This is a borderline case.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is a small back-view prop with only 7 distinct colours, against 11-40 for the references (bench 14, lamp 14, hedge 11, stall 40, well 38). Its colours-per-tile median is 7, below the hedge at 10 and well below the stall at 17 and the well at 20. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas, and the outline reads as a tinted dark brown (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which fits the dark-material-tone approach. Because the piece is thin, the density fact counts only lightly, but by eye it is still a step below the references, and since the guidance says to fail when in doubt, it fails.

answer.evidence: Seen from behind. Rows 10-13 form a lit top band (L rises 128→171→195) with a bright edge line at row 13. Darker shadow rows 14-15 follow, then a 10-row back face (rows 16-25) with slats. A second lighter band at rows 19-21, with an edge line at row 21 and shadow at rows 22-23, suggests the seat. Legs occupy rows 26-29. The width profile (12 → 14 → 8 → 4) is a standing object with a top and a deep front face, not a flat slab or a side elevation. The top band is only about 4 rows, so this is a borderline top surface, but it is more than a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The chair has only 7 distinct colours, against 14 for the bench and lamp, 11 for the hedge, and 38-40 for the stall and well. Its wood ramp has about 4 steps (a light tan back, a mid tan, a darker brown and a dark brown edge), where the bench and the richer references use 5-6. The outline passes: 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so it is a tinted dark brown beside the wood, not a black sticker line. There are no flat 5x5 fills (0% coverage). But the back slats and seat show little grain, no per-plank highlights and no texture dots, so the surface reads as clean and simple. The median per-tile colour count of 7 is below the hedge (10), stall (17) and well (20). This is a thin furniture prop, so I weigh that fact lightly. By eye, though, the chair still looks flatter and thinner than the bench beside it, which has a highlighted slat top and a shaded underside. A careful artist would likely ask for more ramp steps and grain, so it fails by a narrow margin.
